anti_overlap: Focuses on choice architecture and conversion, not visual aesthetics or technical implementation
decision_lens: Choice architecture — does the layout guide visitors toward the highest-value action?
distance_rationale: Menu engineers optimize information presentation for decision-making under time pressure — same challenge as a landing page
expected_isomorphisms: Visual anchoring, choice reduction, benefit-oriented labeling, scan-pattern optimization
focus: Menu engineering principles applied to landing page layout — choice architecture, attention anchoring, and conversion optimization
name: fd-restaurant-menu-engineering
persona: Hospitality consultant who designs restaurant menus to optimize both customer satisfaction and revenue
review_areas: Visual anchor points — where does the eye land first on the landing page?
Choice overload — does the portal offer too many options or the right number?
Decoy effect — is the wiki link positioned as the obvious best choice?
Section naming — do labels describe benefits or just categories?
Scan patterns — does the layout work for both F-pattern scanners and deep readers?
Price of attention — what's the cognitive cost to reach the wiki from the landing page?

severity_examples.scenario: Landing page has 8+ equal-weight links with no visual hierarchy
Section labels are generic (Features, Links) instead of benefit-oriented

success_hints: Landing page has a clear visual hierarchy that guides visitors to the wiki (primary) and other resources (secondary) without decision paralysis
task_context: The landing page is a choice architecture problem — visitors need to choose where to go, and the design should make the right choice obvious
